articles.title: State's largest mosque leader’s deportation fight takes dramatic turn as Trump admin scores major win
articles.summary: Marco Rubio ordered the deportation of Milwaukee's largest mosque leader on national security grounds, citing Israeli convictions and alleged terror ties.
articles.body:
Immigration judge rules that leader of Wisconsin’s largest mosque can be deported on national security grounds, citing decades-old convictions in Israel.

Government lawyers argue that Salah Sarsour poses a national security threat due to past convictions for throwing rocks at Israeli military personnel and attempting to procure weapons.

Sarsour, who has been a lawful permanent resident in the U.S. for over 30 years, claims he is being targeted by the Trump administration for political reasons related to his advocacy on the Israel-Gaza conflict.

An immigration judge ruled Wednesday that federal authorities can deport the leader of Wisconsin's largest mosque on national security grounds.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio invoked federal immigration law in June 2025 to determine that Salah Sarsour, the president of the Islamic Society of Milwaukee, could be deported because his presence in the United States could have potentially serious adverse foreign policy consequences. Government lawyers cited Sarsour's decades-old convictions in Israel, including for throwing rocks at Israeli military personnel and attempting to procure weapons, in arguing that he posed a national security threat.

Government lawyers also claimed he had been convicted of throwing a Molotov cocktail at IDF personnel, though Sarsour's lawyer rebuffed that allegation by stating that, though he was accused of doing so, he was never convicted.

"If a lawful resident of the United States for over 30 years with zero arrests or convictions in this country, a family man and the father of 6 U.S. citizen kids, the elected president of his mosque, and an advocate for interfaith dialogue is a 'public safety threat,' as DHS claims, those words cease to have any meaning at all," Patrick Taurel, a lawyer representing Sarsour, told Fox News Digital.

A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson told Fox News Digital that Rubio had "reasonable grounds to believe Sarsour's presence would have adverse foreign policy consequences for the U.S., and he has engaged in terrorist activity or supported a terrorist organization."

A 2001 FBI memorandum summarized allegations from Sarsour's brother, Jamil, that he had been involved in fundraising for the Holy Land Foundation , an organization shuttered by the federal government for terror ties, on behalf of Hamas. Jewish Insider, meanwhile, reported that Sarsour wrote a Facebook post asking God to "give Gaza people victory," while acknowledging in a deposition that additional language in the post could be translated as asking God to punish those who wished harm on Gaza.

"Under President Trump and Secretary Mullin , if you break the law, you will face the consequences. Criminal illegal aliens are not welcome in the U.S.," the DHS spokesperson told Fox News Digital, adding that "illegal aliens receive due process."

Sarsour, who is a lawful permanent resident according to court documents, and his lawyers claim that he is being targeted by the Trump administration for political reasons, namely his advocacy related to the Israel-Gaza conflict. He also claims that he was tortured into providing a confession by Israeli authorities.

Sarsour's lawyers also point out that he has been residing in the country for 30 years, questioning why the government waited so long to seek his removal if he was a threat to national security.

Sarsour has pledged to appeal the judge's ruling that he can be deported.

"I will continue fighting to defend the right to free speech and to stay in the country I have called home for more than three decades," he said in a statement following the judge's ruling.

articles.title: Snap, clap, twirl into the garba spirit
articles.summary: With Navratri just a fortnight away, NCR residents' weekday evenings and weekends are getting a festive spin as dance enthusiasts learn garba and raas
articles.body: With Navratri just a fortnight away, NCR residents' weekday evenings and weekends are getting a festive spin as dance enthusiasts learn garba and raas from experts. Planning to head to a garba night during Navratri? Brush up on the basics so you can snap-clap-twirl and keep pace with the circle during these community celebrations.'Garba isn’t about perfection'At Lok Utsav Foundation, director Yamini Dikshit says the learning process is similarly structured to take beginners from basic movements to fuller sequences. “Garba is not about performing perfectly; it is about participating and enjoying the experience. Our one-month workshop follows a gradual learning process, beginning with basic hand and leg movements before moving to six Garba and five Dandiya sequences. Towards the end, we introduce formations such as heench and teen taali.”Yamini adds, "One thing we consciously maintain is the authenticity of the dance form. While we do use a variety of music, from traditional Garba compositions to carefully selected Bollywood tracks, we don't believe in changing the fundamental character of Garba simply to follow a trend. Our choreography continues to be rooted in traditional movements and steps. At the same time, our participants have evolved over the years. Those who have been with us since the early days now often look forward to more complex, faster-paced movements because they have developed a strong foundation. On the other hand, participants who may prefer a slower pace look for simpler movements. As instructors, we try to strike a balance between the two, creating choreography that is challenging enough for experienced dancers while remaining accessible to beginners. The biggest takeaway is perhaps that Garba is not about performing perfectly, it is about participating and enjoying the experience. For many of our students, the workshop becomes a much-needed break from their everyday schedules. They come in after work, college or school, spend an hour dancing, meeting people and learning something new, and leave feeling energised. Over time, the classroom becomes a community, and many participants form friendships and memories that go beyond the workshop itself."Professional dancer Ishita Choudhary, who is learning the form for the first time, shares, “Mujhe FOMO ho raha tha, so I joined the classes. I love the fact that everyone is in a whole circle, doing the same thing. There’s this amazing synergy when everyone is moving together.”Garba instructor Jahnvi Doshi from Thangaat Garba shares, “What makes the response particularly special is the diversity of participants. People from different communities and backgrounds are coming together to learn Garba, discover its culture and experience the infectious energy of dancing as a community.” Doshi adds, “The response reflects how Garba is becoming a more inclusive cultural experience.”‘Keeping it simple, authentic so more people can access this cultural experience’Across centres, garba sessions are bringing together first-timers, seasoned dancers, children and older participants, all working through the steps ahead of Navratri. Choreographer Bharat Singh Rajawat, who has been teaching garba in Delhi for 15 years through his venture Garbaholics 360, has simplified his choreography this year. “Our focus this year is to keep it simple. I have kept the moves very easy and have focused on authenticity so that more people can access this cultural experience.”Delhi-based choreographer Manpreet Singh, founder of Moksha Performing Arts, who conducts classes across South Delhi, shares, “Garba is traditionally a form of devotion to Maa Amba, performed to folk aartis and devotional music. In my classes, I try to keep that authenticity alive by using Gujarati garba songs, teaching traditional steps and then bringing everyone into the circle, which is the traditional format. At the same time, I understand that the Delhi audience enjoys trending music, so I occasionally add viral Garba songs and create engaging combinations with my students.”From nostalgia to workout: Different reasons bring people to garba classesGarba classes are becoming a bridge between different experiences. Harshit Kakaria, an artist who grew up in Ahmedabad, misses the scale of celebrations back home. In Delhi, joining classes has given him a way to reconnect with the culture. “Being away from home, it’s good that I get to explore the garba culture here as well,” he says.Meanwhile, Sanchay Chaudhary, a banker from Mumbai, shares, “It’s a nice workout, and it also helps me freshen up after a hectic day,” he says. Nanvar Hrangkhawl, a college student from Tripura shares, “When you perform in a group, there is this collective happiness that you get to share in a circle. It’s really fun”For others, learning the steps is also about reclaiming a part of their own cultural identity. “My Gujarati side comes alive during these nine days,” says Mansi Parmar, who has grown up in Delhi, who wanted to sharpen her technique. “I saw how the workshop instructor gives shape to the steps, something that I, as a Gujarati, also wanted to improve.”You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Caiado nega apoio a Flávio Bolsonaro no 1º turno | G1
articles.standfirst: Ronaldo Caiado disse que jamais cogitou desistir da própria candidatura. Eleições estão marcadas para domingo (4), e candidato cumpre agenda em Goiás.
articles.summary: Ronaldo Caiado nega ter cogitado apoiar Flávio Bolsonaro no primeiro turno e afirma que não recebeu pedido nesse sentido.
articles.body:
Ronaldo Caiado cumpre agenda em Goiânia — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

O candidato do PSD à Presidência, Ronaldo Caiado, negou neste sábado (3) que apoiará Flávio Bolsonaro ainda no primeiro turno das eleições de 2026. Ele afirmou que a possibilidade de desistir da própria candidatura 'jamais' foi cogitada e que a palavra 'desistir' não faz parte de sua trajetória política.

“É uma luta que fala por milhões de pessoas, não só em Goiás, mas no Brasil. Jamais essa posição sequer foi cogitada comigo. A palavra renúncia, a palavra capitular, a palavra desistir, ela não existe na trajetória de vida do Caiado, que tem 40 anos de enfrentamento. Então isso não existe e jamais essa posição sequer foi cogitada comigo”, afirmou o candidato.

A resposta foi dada após Caiado, que cumpre agenda em Goiás, ser questionado sobre pedidos feitos por integrantes da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro para que ele o apoiasse ainda no primeiro turno das eleições. O candidato também afirmou que não recebeu nenhum pedido nesse sentido.

“Olha, primeiro, não teve essa palavra dele nesse sentido a mim. Até porque todas as pessoas me respeitam, sabem da minha trajetória de vida, e a luta nossa significa aqui não uma luta da pessoa Ronaldo Caiado. É uma luta que fala por milhões de pessoas, tá certo? Não só em Goiás, mas no Brasil.”

Caiado cumpre agenda em Goiânia neste sábado (3) e finaliza o dia com o encerramento da campanha em Trindade , na Região Metropolitana de Goiânia.

articles.summary: A chuva no Rio de Janeiro causa interdições em Botafogo e alagamentos na Zona Sul, com previsão de tempo instável e temperaturas baixas durante todo o sábado.
articles.body:
O Rio de Janeiro registrou chuvas que variaram entre moderadas e fortes desde as primeiras horas da madrugada deste sábado (3).

Até as 10h20, o Recreio dos Bandeirantes e a Barra da Tijuca, na Região Sudoeste do Rio, registravam as maiores concentrações de chuva, além de Copacabana, na Zona Sul.

Bolsão d'água no Jardim Botânico — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Bolsões d'água foram registrados em várias partes da Zona Sul. Na altura do Parque Lage, no Jardim Botânico, motoristas e pedestres enfrentavam dificuldades.

Árvore caiu na rua São Clemente por volta das 5h — Foto: Reprodução

Na rua São Clemente, em Botafogo, uma árvore caiu na rua São Clemente, na altura do morro Santa Marta, por volta das 5h.

Queda de árvore ocorreu na madrugada deste sábado em Botafogo — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Até as 10h10, a via permanecia interditada na altura da Rua da Matriz. O desvio do trânsito estava sendo feito para a rua Dona Mariana.

A Defesa Civil Estadual enviou alertas de chuvas moderadas a fortes para as regiões Baixada Litorânea, Noroeste, Norte e Serrana; e de precipitações fracas a moderadas para as regiões Costa Verde, Sul, Capital, Baixada Fluminense e Metropolitana.

Também foram enviados alertas de rajadas de vento moderado a ocasionalmente forte, a partir da tarde de hoje, para os municípios das regiões Costa Verde, Sul, Capital, Baixada Fluminense, Metropolitana, Baixada Litorânea e Norte.

A previsão do tempo para este sábado (3) para a capital é de tempo chuvoso durante o dia e à noite. As máximas são de 22ºC e as mínimas de 19ºC. Em Niterói , São Gonçalo , Duque de Caxias e Nova Iguaçu , o panorama se repete.

articles.title: Noroeste de SP registra 60% dos casos de leishmaniose no estado  | G1
articles.standfirst: Dos 22 casos confirmados no Estado de São Paulo, 12 foram nas regiões de São José do Rio Preto e Araçatuba (SP).
articles.summary: O noroeste de São Paulo registrou 60% dos casos de leishmaniose do estado em 2026. A região teve 12 dos 22 casos e um óbito.
articles.body:
Mais da metade dos casos de leishmaniose registrados no Estado de São Paulo em 2026 está concentrada na região noroeste, além da confirmação de dois óbitos em território paulista, um deles em Fernandópolis .

Segundo apurado pela reportagem da TV TEM , 12 dos 22 casos relatados pelo governo, ou seja, cerca de 60% do total, ocorreram nas regiões de São José do Rio Preto e Araçatuba .

Transmissão da leishmaniose é feita pelo Mosquito-palha — Foto: Divulgação

Uma pesquisa feita pelo Grupo de Vigilância Epidemiológica (GVE) apontou que, ao longo de 2025, foram contabilizados 12 casos da doença no noroeste paulista, 15 a menos em comparação com o mesmo período de 2024.

Veja as cidades afetadas pela doença em 2026:

Fernandópolis (2 casos, sendo um óbito);

A região de Araçatuba é historicamente uma das mais atingidas. Em anos anteriores, chegou a registrar 37 casos, quatro óbitos em 2022 e 33 casos e três óbitos em 2018.

Imagem microscópica mostra células de mamíferos infectadas com o parasita da Leishmaniose — Foto: Pesquisa/Instituto Adolfo Lutz

A leishmaniose visceral é uma doença infecciosa grave causada pelo protozoário leishmania infantum (ou chagasi).

A transmissão ocorre quando fêmeas do inseto conhecido como mosquito-palha pica cães ou outros animais infectados e, em seguida, pica seres humanos, transmitindo o protozoário.

O inseto costuma se reproduzir em locais com acúmulo de matéria orgânica, como os que contêm folhas secas, restos de frutas, fezes de animais e sujeira em quintais. Se não for tratada, a doença pode ser fatal em até 90% dos casos.

Feridas no focinho, nas orelhas e nas patas.

Como não existe uma vacina única para a prevenção humana, os cuidados devem ser focados no combate ao vetor:

Eliminar possíveis criadouros do mosquito-palha, como retirar matéria orgânica do quintal e não deixar lixo acumulado;

Limpar ambientes que tenham fezes de animais;

Implantar telas nas janelas quando o bicho fica dentro de casa;

Evitar passeios noturnos com os animais. Ao anoitecer, o mosquito apresenta maior atividade.

Prefeitura de Votuporanga (SP) — Foto: Foto: Prefeitura de Votuporanga

Em municípios com novos casos registrados, como Votuporanga, as equipes de saúde realizam vistorias nas residências vizinhas ao local onde houve um foco da doença para identificar e eliminar potenciais criadouros.

A transmissão ocorre pela picada do mosquito-palha, que se reproduz em locais com acúmulo de matéria orgânica (folhas secas, restos de frutas e sujeira em quintais).

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro faz motocarreata com Tarcísio no interior de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato à Presidência da República está acompanhado também dos candidatos ao Senado por São Paulo André do Prado (PL) e Guilherme Derrite (PP).
articles.summary: Candidato à Presidência da República está acompanhado também dos candidatos ao Senado por São Paulo André do Prado (PL) e Guilherme Derrite (PP).
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) iniciou o último dia de campanha para o primeiro turno das eleições de 2026 com uma motocarreata entre Santa Bárbara d'Oeste (SP) e Americana (SP) na manhã deste sábado (3).

O candidato à Presidência da República está acompanhado do governador de São Paulo e candidato à reeleição, Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), e dos candidatos ao Senado pelo estado André do Prado (PL) e Guilherme Derrite (PP).

O percurso começou por volta das 11h, saindo de Santa Bárbara e seguindo pela Rodovia Anhanguera (SP-330), até chegar ao recinto da Festa do Peão de Americana, às 12h30.

"Vê se isso aqui não é sinal de vitória no primeiro turno. Obrigado, São Paulo, obrigado, Brasil. Faltam poucas horas para a gente libertar nosso Brasil", disse Flávio mostrando o público que acompanha o candidato na motocarreata em uma transmissão nas redes sociais durante o trajeto.

No período da tarde, Flávio Bolsonaro tem programada uma outra carreata no Rio de Janeiro.

articles.title: Milhares de pessoas protestam na Espanha contra crise habitacional | G1
articles.standfirst: Protestos ocorrem após Parlamento rejeitar medidas do governo para enfrentar a crise habitacional; em Madri, cerca de 70 mil pessoas participaram do ato.
articles.summary: Parlamento rejeitou medidas do governo para enfrentar o problema; em Madri, cerca de 70 mil pessoas participaram do ato.
articles.body:
Manifestantes protestam por medidas para conter despejos e aliviar a crise habitacional em Madri, Espanha, em 3 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Juan Barbosa

Dezenas de milhares de pessoas foram às ruas de Madri e de outras cidades espanholas neste sábado (3) para cobrar medidas contra a crescente crise habitacional . Os protestos ocorreram um dia após o Parlamento rejeitar propostas apresentadas pelo governo.

Alguns manifestantes carregavam cartazes pedindo uma greve geral. As medidas rejeitadas haviam sido elaboradas após a revolta provocada pelo despejo de uma mulher de 87 anos em Madri e em meio a outros problemas relacionados à moradia.

“É uma vergonha”, disse Nando de Anguulo, de 26 anos, que participou do protesto em Madri. “Isso só prova que somos nós, o povo, que temos de nos adaptar aos partidos políticos, e não os políticos ao que o povo quer. E isso não pode continuar assim.”

O primeiro-ministro espanhol, Pedro Sánchez , poderá convocar uma eleição antecipada em novembro após o projeto ser rejeitado pelo Parlamento , informou a imprensa espanhola na sexta-feira (2).

Segundo os relatos, Sánchez estaria acompanhando a dimensão dos protestos deste sábado antes de tomar uma decisão.

O gabinete de Sánchez não quis comentar as informações. Na cidade de Valência , no sudeste do país, manifestantes entraram em confronto com a polícia, que usou balas de borracha e gás lacrimogêneo para dispersar o ato.

Cerca de 30 manifestantes conseguiram entrar na Cidade das Artes e das Ciências, um importante complexo cultural local, mas foram retirados pela polícia. Outras manifestações em 50 cidades espanholas ocorreram de forma pacífica.

Valeria Racu, porta-voz da União dos Inquilinos, disse a jornalistas em Madri que uma greve geral será convocada após negociações com os sindicatos.

Segundo o governo espanhol, cerca de 70 mil pessoas participaram do ato realizado neste sábado (3) em Madri.

Os protestos previstos para Barcelona e para a cidade vizinha de L'Hospitalet de Llobregat foram cancelados devido às fortes chuvas .

articles.title: ‘Recebi meu filho em uma sacola’, diz mãe de menino autista na BA | G1
articles.standfirst: Caso aconteceu em Alagoinhas. Segundo a mãe, escola alegou que mandou menino em sacola para evitar sujar de fezes o carro da prefeitura.
articles.summary: Caso aconteceu em Alagoinhas. Segundo a mãe, escola alegou que mandou menino em sacola para evitar sujar de fezes o carro da prefeitura.
articles.body:
Criança autista foi enviada para casa pela escola dentro de saco plástico e com fralda suja na Bahia — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

“Nenhuma mãe espera receber seu filho em casa da forma em que eu o recebi, vestido em uma sacola”. O relato é de Camila de Jesus Almeida, mãe de um menino de seis anos, diagnosticado com Transtorno do Espectro Autista (TEA), que foi enviado para casa dentro de uma sacola plástica e com a fralda cheia de fezes por uma escola municipal de Alagoinhas , no interior da Bahia.

O caso aconteceu em 24 de setembro, na Escola Municipal de Educação Integral do Campo. Segundo a mãe, a escola informou à família que a criança seria levada para casa porque não havia fralda e roupa disponíveis para fazer a troca. Camila, no entanto, afirma que os itens estavam na mochila do filho.

Em entrevista à TV Subaé, afiliada da Rede Bahia na região, a mãe mostrou a sacola usada para levar o menino para casa.

“Está aqui o lugar onde cortaram no saco plástico para que ele colocassem as perninhas dentro. Foi neste saco que a gestão mandou meu filho vestido para casa. Foi um susto, um desespero”, relatou.

Segundo Camila, a mãe dela foi quem recebeu o menino em casa. Ao verificar a mochila, ela encontrou uma fralda e a roupa limpa que poderiam ter sido utilizadas para fazer a troca.

“Minha mãe verificou a mochila dele e lá dentro estava a fralda e a roupa limpa para que fosse feita a troca. Não tinha justificativa ou motivo para mandar ele dessa forma”, afirmou.

Camila de Jesus Almeida contou como filho foi enviado para casa dentro de saco plástico — Foto: Rogenis Dias | TV Subaé

Ainda conforme a mãe, ela entrou em contato com a direção da escola logo após saber do ocorrido e questionou o motivo de o filho ter sido colocado dentro da sacola. Segundo Camila, a diretora afirmou que havia sido responsável pela decisão e que fez isso para evitar que o menino sujasse o carro da Secretaria Municipal de Educação.

“Eu disse que não aceitava nem admitia. Meu filho foi humilhado”, contou.

A mãe também destacou que o menino é autista não verbal e, por isso, não teria condições de relatar o que havia acontecido.

“Ele tem transtorno do espectro autista, não verbal. Ele não teve o direito de dizer que não queria ser colocado naquela situação”, disse.

Criança autista foi enviada para casa pela escola dentro de saco plástico e com fralda suja na Bahia — Foto: Rogenis Dias | TV Subaé

Após o episódio, Camila procurou a Secretaria Municipal de Educação para denunciar a situação. Ela também registrou um boletim de ocorrência e informou ter levado o caso ao Ministério Público da Bahia (MP-BA), ao Conselho Municipal da Pessoa com Deficiência e ao Conselho Tutelar.

Segundo a mãe, a família já havia enfrentado outras situações semelhantes. Ela afirmou que o episódio ocorrido em setembro não teria sido a primeira vez que o menino teria sido enviado para casa após se sujar.

A Polícia Civil informou que investiga a denúncia de constrangimento e que diligências e oitivas estão em andamento para esclarecer o caso.

Em nota, a Prefeitura de Alagoinhas, por meio da Secretaria Municipal de Educação (Seduc), informou que adotou as providências administrativas cabíveis diante da ocorrência envolvendo uma criança matriculada na Escola Municipal de Educação Integral do Campo. A Secretaria realizou a escuta da família e dos profissionais envolvidos para averiguar as circunstâncias do caso e reunir as informações necessárias à apuração.

Diante da natureza da ocorrência, os relatos e documentos coletados foram encaminhados ao setor jurídico da Prefeitura de Alagoinhas para instauração de sindicância, para apurar os fatos e verificar eventual responsabilidade funcional.

A Prefeitura de Alagoinhas disse que reitera seu compromisso com a segurança, a proteção e o bem-estar dos estudantes da rede municipal. Diante do ocorrido, o Governo Municipal informa que acompanha o caso de perto e adotará todas as providências cabíveis até a sua devida conclusão.

O g1 entrou em contato com o Ministério Público (MP-BA) sobre o ocorrido e aguarda retorno.

articles.title: Falta de energia provoca congestionamento em praça de pedágio de MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Way-262 informou que praça entrou em situação de contingência e operação precisou ser feita manualmente. Atendimento foi restabelecido com apoio de gerador, mas fornecimento de energia ainda não foi normalizado.
articles.summary: Way-262 informou que praça entrou em situação de contingência e operação precisou ser feita manualmente. Atendimento foi restabelecido com apoio de gerador.
articles.body:
Congestionamento ocorreu por falta de energia em Pará de Minas — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Uma interrupção no fornecimento de energia elétrica provocou congestionamento na praça de pedágio da BR-262 , em Pará de Minas , na noite desta sexta-feira (2). A operação precisou ser realizada manualmente para garantir a liberação dos veículos e reduzir os impactos no trânsito.

Segundo a Way-262, concessionária responsável pelo trecho, a praça entrou em situação de contingência durante a falta de energia . A empresa não informou quanto tempo durou o período de contingência nem a extensão do congestionamento.

Ainda conforme a concessionária, o sistema da praça já foi restabelecido e funciona normalmente com o apoio de um gerador .

O fornecimento de energia elétrica pela Companhia Energética de Minas Gerais (Cemig), no entanto, ainda não foi normalizado. O g1 solicitou um posicionamento da Cemig e aguarda retorno.

A Way-262 informou que acompanha a situação e mantém a operação no local para garantir a segurança e a fluidez do trânsito.

articles.title: Augusto Cury critica privilégios políticos em fim de campanha | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato a presidente do Avante fez último dia de campanha do primeiro turno em Colina (SP), onde nasceu.
articles.summary: Em Colina, o candidato do Avante Augusto Cury encerrou sua campanha criticando gastos da elite política e se apresentando como alternativa para o Brasil.
articles.body:
O candidato à presidência da República Augusto Cury (Avante) criticou neste sábado (3) o excesso de privilégios dos políticos que estão no poder enquanto professores convivem com a falta de estrutura em sala de aula.

"O Lula da Silva tem 74 funcionários do Palácio da Alvorada na sua casa. O Flávio Bolsonaro tem mais de 40 assessores e quem paga a conta, quem paga a conta é o contribuinte. E um professor não tem um auxiliar dentro da sala de aula e ele tem o ouro da humanidade lá em sala de aula. Isso está errado, isso é uma vergonha", afirmou.

O escritor de 68 anos realizou seu último dia de campanha do primeiro turno das eleições 2026 em Colina (SP), cidade de 18,9 mil habitantes da região de Ribeirão Preto (SP) onde nasceu.

Augusto Cury durante caminhada em Colina (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Durante a caminhada pelas ruas, ele abraçou apoiadores e visitou uma padaria, onde comeu pão com mortadela e lembrou da origem humilde. Cury disse ser uma alternativa aos candidatos que lideram as pesquisas de intenção de voto.

"Quero devolver o sonho para o brasileiro, porque é uma vergonha lá em Brasília, a elite política esqueceu da sociedade brasileira, as pessoas reais que precisam ser abraçadas. (...) O Brasil tem cura. Nem picanha, nem fuzil, é Cury para o Brasil."

Cury durante caminhada em Colina (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Durante entrevista coletiva, Augusto Cury voltou a criticar o cenário de polarização política no país e disse que sonha em ser presidente do Brasil para mudar a vida das pessoas.

"Voltei às minhas origens, onde meus sonhos, eles impactaram dezenas de milhões de pessoas em mais de 90 países. E agora eu sonho com a presidência da República. Não porque eu amo o poder, vou doar o meu salário, mas porque o Brasil merece paz. Só a paz é capaz de vencer o ódio da polarização", afirmou.

Segundo ele, se eleito, vai chamar os melhores especialistas para governar a nação, que vive um momento de colapso, nas palavras dele.

"Estou fazendo para que as crianças e adolescentes, bem como o comerciante, o agricultor, as famílias, essas mulheres possam ter um futuro nesse país, porque o Brasil está colapsando. Estamos derretendo econômica, eticamente, estamos derretendo socialmente. Nós precisamos voltar a sonhar."

articles.title: Southeastern trains cancelled after bedbugs found on board
articles.summary: Southeastern said the insects were discovered in drivers' cabs, with the trains removed for cleaning.
articles.body:
A number of train services were cancelled after drivers discovered bedbugs in their cabs.

Carriages on two affected trains were locked to isolate passenger areas from the cabs, said Southeastern, which operates services in Kent, East Sussex and Greater London.

The rail firm said the trains only remained in service while they "returned to a suitable location for inspection and if necessary, treatment".

The cancellations took place on mainline routes after the bugs were spotted on 22 September. None of the insects were found on any High Speed 1 trains, it added.

In a social media post, Southeastern said the affected trains were based at the West Marina Depot in Hastings, the terminus point for trains from London.

Services on the route go via Battle, Tunbridge Wells and Sevenoaks.

A spokesperson for the firm said trains and stations are cleaned "thoroughly" so passengers can "travel safely and with confidence".

Oly Turner, head of drivers at Southeastern, said: "We have a great relationship with our drivers, who have helped hugely in cooperating with us over these isolated incidents.

"When we receive reports such as these we check trains thoroughly before they are put back into service when given the all clear.

"Cases have been contained to the drivers' cabs in only two of our trains and no bed bugs have been identified in areas for passengers."

articles.title: Morley's derelict church St Mary's In The Wood sold at auction
articles.summary: St Mary's In The Wood United Reformed Church on Commercial Street in Morley sells for £100,000.
articles.body:
A derelict Grade II listed church located in a wooded area of Leeds has been sold at auction.

St Mary's In The Wood United Reformed Church on Commercial Street in Morley sold for £100,000 earlier this week, auctioneers BTG Eddisons confirmed.

The 19th Century building has not been used for worship since 2008 and fell into disrepair after sustaining extensive fire damage two years later.

A previous planning application lodged with Leeds City Council which has since lapsed proposed the site could be repurposed into a hotel, restaurant and car park.

Later plans to transform the fire-damaged church into 18 apartments also did not come to fruition.

The fire started about 02:30 BST in June 2010 and caused 20 people living nearby to be evacuated to a nearby supermarket due to fears the church steeple could collapse.

In 2023, Leeds City Council purchased the nearby former Sunday School building, which was built in 1900, for use as a "learning and skills centre".

However, the older, Gothic revival-style building, built in 1878, has remained vacant for more than 15 years.

BTG Eddisons could not disclose whether St Mary's was bought by a commercial or private buyer.

articles.title: Coast Guard searching off Nantucket for medical evacuation jet carrying 6 people heading from Bermuda to Boston
articles.summary: The U.S. Coast Guard is searching for a Gulfstream jet carrying six people that lost contact with flight controllers Saturday morning on its way to Boston from the island of Bermuda.
articles.body: The U.S. Coast Guard is searching for a Gulfstream jet carrying six people that lost contact with flight controllers Saturday morning on its way to Boston from the island of Bermuda. The Coast Guard says air and surface crews have launched in search of the aircraft, a Gulfstream G100 jet. The plane was carrying out a medical evacuation in Bermuda, said Clarence Togeretz, the director of flight operations at Latitude Air Ambulance, which operates the plane. “We always get rather concerned when our crew doesn’t report to us in a timely manner,” he told NBC News. “But I will say that again, optimistically and positively, that doesn’t mean that the worst has happened.” Togeretz added that Latitude Air Ambulance has an emergency response plan in place “absolutely for anything that might occur to any of our missions.” The Massachusetts Port Authority, which operates Boston Logan International Airport, said the aircraft did not arrive as scheduled. A spokesperson said: “Our thoughts are with those on board and their loved ones as the search continues.” Air traffic control tower audio from Boston, obtained by NBC News, appears to indicate that controllers asked the aircraft if it was “coming in blind.” Controllers later ask another plane to “attempt contact” with the jet. It is unclear whether that attempt was successful. The current search area is “off the coast of Nantucket,” the Coast Guard Northeast District said in an update on X. Emergency services audio obtained by NBC News asked vessels to keep a “sharp lookout” for any signs of a “possible aircraft in the water.” Data from Flightradar24 showed a number of aircraft searching south of the island. The Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement that it issued a search-and-rescue notice for the jet at 1:20 a.m. ET on Saturday, and is coordinating with the Coast Guard and Rescue Coordination Center to locate the aircraft. Bermuda is a British overseas territory in the North Atlantic, about 650 miles from North Carolina.

articles.title: New York men cut 4 trees on neighbour’s land after being warned about property line, then face $35,000 court award
articles.summary: A property-line dispute in New York escalated into a court battle after two men entered a neighbour’s land and removed trees and vegetation despite being
articles.body: A property-line dispute in New York escalated into a court battle after two men entered a neighbour’s land and removed trees and vegetation despite being shown a survey identifying the disputed boundary. Nicholas Howard and Micah Geraghty were involved in the October 2021 incident in Columbia County, where four trees on Elaine Storms’ property were removed. Storms had previously shown the men a survey indicating where she believed the property line stood, and another neighbour later confirmed the same boundary. Despite that, the men returned about two weeks later and partially cleared the area. A jury initially awarded $55,000 in punitive damages, but the amount was later reduced and ultimately restored in part by an appeals court.New York's property-line dispute escalatesThe dispute began after Howard purchased property next to Storms’ land in June 2021. By October, the parties were arguing over the location of the boundary between the properties. During a heated disagreement on October 11, Storms showed Howard and Geraghty a survey that placed the property line where she said it was. The men later spoke with another neighbour, who also confirmed the boundary.According to the evidence described by the Appellate Division, the men nevertheless returned roughly two weeks later. They used equipment to partially clear a lot they still incorrectly believed belonged to Howard, without first taking steps to independently establish the correct property line. The clearing resulted in the removal of trees and vegetation from Storms’ property.Four trees were removedStorms subsequently sued, alleging trespass, damage to real property under New York’s Real Property Actions and Proceedings Law and seeking to establish ownership of the disputed portion of land.At trial, the jury found that Howard and Geraghty had entered Storms’ property without permission. It also specifically found that four trees had been cut, removed, injured or destroyed without Storms’ permission, or that the defendants had caused this to happen.The jury awarded $3,000 against each defendant under the state law relating to damage to trees, with the money intended to cover restoration costs. The court record said the restoration estimate presented at trial was $14,330, potentially rising to $20,330 if additional drainage work was required.Storms said the damage went beyond the treesThe case involved more than the loss of four trees. Storms testified that the clearing affected drainage on her property and removed tree cover and vegetation that had provided privacy.She presented evidence that estimated the property’s value had fallen from $335,000 to $285,000 following the defendants’ actions. She also said the incident caused her stress and aggravation.However, despite finding that Storms had suffered actual damage from the trespass, the jury awarded $0 in compensatory damages on the trespass claim. Instead, it found that the defendants’ conduct was wanton and reckless or malicious and awarded punitive damages of $40,000 against Geraghty and $15,000 against Howard.Judge cuts $55,000 punitive award to just $6The case then took an unusual turn. Because the jury had awarded no compensatory damages for the trespass claim, the trial court modified the verdict by awarding $1 in nominal damages against each defendant.It then reduced the punitive damages from $40,000 against Geraghty and $15,000 against Howard to just $3 against each man. The court concluded that the original punitive awards were excessive under constitutional due-process standards because they were vastly greater than the nominal compensatory damages.That left the defendants with a combined judgment of $8,008, including other damages connected to the tree-removal claim.Appeals court restores $35,000Storms appealed, arguing that reducing the punitive damages to $3 each effectively stripped the punishment of any meaningful effect.On May 14, 2026, New York’s Appellate Division, Third Department agreed that the original $55,000 punitive award was excessive, but it also concluded that the trial court had gone too far in reducing the amount to what it described as a token sum.The appeals court noted that the defendants had been given information about the property boundary before returning to clear the land. It also said their actions involved aggravating circumstances, including failing to make further efforts to establish the boundary and intentionally interfering with Storms’ property rights.The court ultimately set punitive damages at $25,000 against Geraghty and $10,000 against Howard, for a combined $35,000.Court says $3 each would not deter future misconductThe appeals court explained that punitive damages are intended not only to punish wrongful conduct but also to deter similar behaviour in the future. It said requiring each defendant to pay only $3 would not meaningfully accomplish either purpose.The court also pointed to New York’s tree-protection law, which permits statutory damages for the unauthorised cutting or destruction of trees. Under the relevant provision, the statute allows damages based on the tree’s value or a specified amount per tree, along with compensation for permanent and substantial damage to land or improvements.Final rulingThe Appellate Division therefore modified the judgments, increasing the punitive damages to $25,000 against Geraghty and $10,000 against Howard while otherwise affirming the judgments.The case is notable because a dispute involving just four trees produced a complicated legal battle over property boundaries, trespass, punitive damages and constitutional limits on civil penalties. The final $35,000 punitive award was substantially lower than the jury’s original $55,000 award, but far higher than the $6 imposed by the trial court.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Dual U.K.-Iranian national released on bail over suspected plot against U.S.-run military base
articles.summary: A dual U.K.-Iranian national arrested on suspicion of plotting a terror attack following a security incident at a U.S.-run military air base in England has been released on bail, authorities said Saturday.
articles.body: A dual U.K.-Iranian national arrested on suspicion of plotting a terror attack following a security incident at a U.S.-run military air base in England has been released on bail, authorities said Saturday. The 25-year-old man was arrested Thursday in London on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts close to the RAF Fairford air base, which has been used by American bombers to strike Iran. He was the sixth person taken into custody and then released on bail as detectives investigate the incident. British authorities have linked the incident to Tehran. The five other men were not named, but police said they are all British nationals in their 20s and from London. Scores of residents were evacuated from their homes near the base early Sunday as armed police officers and army bomb-disposal experts swooped on the rural area. Police later said they had found a quantity of an accelerant — gasoline — in three vans linked to the five suspects, but no explosives. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said the U.K. sees “strong indications” that Iran played a part in the incident. He did not provide details about what the suspects were planning or why the U.K. thinks Iran was involved. Iran has denied involvement. It has previously said that it considers any base used to attack its territory a legitimate target. RAF Fairford, 100 miles west of London, has been used by American bombers during decades of conflicts in the Middle East, including this year’s war with Iran. Top U.S. officials have criticized the decision to grant the five suspects bail, with President Donald Trump saying “I wouldn’t have done that” and Secretary of State Marco Rubio saying a lot of people were “disturbed” by the move. The arrests came at a time of heightened tensions around the threat from hostile states, with British security services saying Russia and Iran have both used proxies to commit crimes on U.K. soil. British officials have said the number of national security cases involving activity by hostile states, including Iran, increased by 50% in the six months to December 2025. U.K. officials say proxies linked to Iran have been behind a string of arsons and other attacks in Britain and other countries, many of them targeting the Jewish community and intended to sow fear. They have previously warned that Tehran could expand its targets in the U.K. if conflicts in the Middle East continue.

articles.title: Israeli settlers attack farmers in West Bank pogrom, soldiers hit reporters
articles.summary: Israeli forces detain and assault journalists in Jabal Qamass area in Beita, south of Nablus.
articles.body:
Israeli settlers under the Israeli army’s protection have attacked olive pickers, burned olive trees and detained dozens of people in the occupied West Bank.

Saturday’s pogroms took place at olive groves in the village of Abu Dis, the town of Awarta and the az-Zahra area in the town of Beita, among other places, according to our colleagues on the ground.

“When we arrived this morning, a group of about 50 masked settlers approached. They were throwing stones and attacked a house,” an activist from California volunteering with Palestinian communities to harvest olives who asked to remain anonymous told Al Jazeera.

“Shortly afterwards, they [the settlers] were followed by soldiers who came and rounded up all the Palestinians and activists who were olive harvesting and told the activists they had to leave. They sat them on the ground at gunpoint and forced us to leave,” the activist added.

Meanwhile, Israeli forces detained journalists and assaulted them in the Jabal Qamass area in Beita, south of Nablus, our colleagues reported.

Al Jazeera footage captured settlers smashing a Palestinian vehicle in Osarin while other videos showed the moment armed settlers attacked a Palestinian home in Beita.

In the village of Osarin in Nablus, they fired tear gas at Palestinians and journalists and attacked homes, stoned vehicles and assaulted several villagers, the Palestinian news agency Wafa said.

Palestinian media reported a number of residents have tried to repel the settler attacks , which are part of a wider pogrom against Palestinians across the West Bank that has intensified since February.

Since Israel launched its genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023, Israelis have killed 1,212 Palestinians in the West Bank, including 254 children. Most of the killings were carried out by soldiers. More than a quarter were committed by settlers.

Palestinian authorities said 30 Palestinians have been killed by settlers since the start of 2026, more than in any year since 2022.

articles.title: 'Most comprehensive plan': Ukraine confirms India playing role in mediating energy truce in Black Sea
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's role in efforts to find a negotiated end to the Russia-Ukraine war has gained greater prominence, with Kyiv describing an Indian
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's role in efforts to find a negotiated end to the Russia-Ukraine war has gained greater prominence, with Kyiv describing an Indian proposal as the most comprehensive among four initiatives currently under discussion and saying New Delhi has, for the first time, indicated its willingness to play an active mediating role.Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha recently said Ukraine was prepared to consider both an energy and agricultural truce in the Black Sea, while also remaining open to an unconditional ceasefire along the line of contact."We have four proposals. The most comprehensive is India's proposal. For the first time, India has signalled its willingness to play a role," Sybiha said during a press briefing, according to RBC Ukraine.India proposal among four initiativesAccording to Sybiha, four proposals are currently being considered in diplomatic efforts surrounding the war.India's proposal was described by the Ukrainian foreign minister as the most comprehensive.Türkiye and Egypt have separately proposed a grain and agricultural truce in the Black Sea, while the United States has put forward an energy truce proposal.The agricultural and maritime component is particularly important for Egypt, which relies on Ukrainian grain for roughly a third of its supply, according to RBC Ukraine.The US proposal on an energy truce was also discussed during a meeting between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and US President Donald Trump.Kyiv has conveyed its own approach to its partners and wants the energy and Black Sea components to be treated as an interconnected package.Sybiha said the energy component would require a complete halt to attacks on energy infrastructure, including port facilities.Ukraine has also expressed readiness for an unconditional ceasefire along the line of contact. Sybiha said such a ceasefire could potentially emerge from a meeting between Zelenskyy and Russian President Vladimir Putin.The US is currently working actively on this diplomatic track, according to the Ukrainian foreign minister.Kyiv backs safe Black Sea shippingThe latest Ukrainian position builds on India's earlier engagement with Kyiv over restoring safe navigation in the Black Sea.During last month's UN General Assembly-related engagements, Zelenskyy said Egypt, India and Türkiye had put forward options for a maritime truce between Russia and Ukraine."We are waiting for Russia's response. Ukraine is ready ... to ensure safe shipping and food security in the Black Sea if Russia is ready to take real steps towards de-escalation too. We have to start somewhere," Zelenskyy said at the time.Also read: India's proposal under consideration for safe Black Sea shipping, Zelenskyy saysIndia has been engaging with both Moscow and Kyiv while advocating dialogue and diplomacy.External affairs minister S Jaishankar had said India was in continuous contact with both sides and was exploring ideas that could help mitigate and eventually end the conflict."If India can be of any help, in any manner, we are there," Jaishankar said during his visit to Kyiv last month.During that visit, Jaishankar met Zelenskyy and Sybiha, with discussions covering peace efforts, bilateral cooperation, Black Sea navigation and global food security.Sybiha had also said Ukraine valued India's engagement in efforts to restore freedom of navigation in the Black Sea."Restoring freedom of navigation is critical for global food security. Ukraine is ready to play a constructive role and we value India’s engagement," he said in a post on X.Russia's position remains key to next stepsWhile Ukraine has indicated its readiness to consider multiple limited ceasefire arrangements, Russia's response remains central to whether the proposals can move forward.Sybiha's comments come amid differing assessments in Europe over Moscow's willingness to enter substantive peace negotiations.German Chancellor Friedrich Merz recently said Russia was not currently interested in genuine peace negotiations, while German foreign minister Johann Wadephul has expressed expectations that talks to end the war could begin in the near future.The Kremlin had previously said there were no prerequisites for moving towards a broader peace negotiating track while maintaining that Russia remained open to talks."For now, there are no prerequisites for moving on to a peaceful negotiating track, although we, as the Russian side, remain open to peace talks," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.Ukraine's latest position therefore places several limited ceasefire proposals, covering energy infrastructure, Black Sea shipping and agricultural supplies, alongside the possibility of a broader unconditional ceasefire along the line of contact.India's proposal is being considered alongside those initiatives, with Sybiha describing it as the most comprehensive and saying New Delhi has now signalled its readiness to play a role in the process.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Over 5,500 trees recorded across Sussex in restoration project
articles.summary: The Lost Woods of the Low Weald and Downs project aims to restore some of Sussex's ancient woodland.
articles.body:
A project which aims to restore ancient woodlands in Sussex has hit a significant "milestone" with over 5,500 trees now recorded.

Since March 2024, volunteers with the Lost Woods project have been recording ancient, veteran and notable trees across a 121-sq-miles (314-sq-km) area from Lewes to Storrington.

According to the latest figures, they have now recorded 5,570 trees, a number which Lost Woods outreach adviser, Bob Epsom, said is more than "we expected" and signifies a "milestone" for the project.

"When we look at the map of it, we can see the new clusters of trees being added...that's where the volunteers have been active," he said.

The Lost Woods is a partnership with four charities: Woodland Trust, Action in Rural Sussex, Sussex Wildlife Trust and Small Woods Association.

The work, funded by the National Lottery Heritage Fund, is part of a wider Lost Woods restoration programme which Epsom said comprises "19 individual projects".

About 20 volunteers are each given a square kilometre area to cover, and once recorded and verified, trees are added to the Ancient Tree Inventory which has been mapping the oldest and most important trees in the UK for 20 years.

The volunteers are working to find and record every ancient and veteran tree in the project area by next year, and Epsom, who leads the team, said they still "have a reasonable amount to cover".

Of the 5,570 trees recorded, there were 348 ancient trees, those that are in the third and final stage of their lives, and 2,467 notable trees, mature trees which are large in comparison with other trees around them.

The biggest proportion of trees, 2,743, are veteran, survivors which have developed some of the features found on ancient trees.

The remainder fall into a different category of tree.

According to Epsom, these trees are "very important for the landscape, (and) very important for biodiversity" because of their fungi.

Epsom said the mapping process was "only the first step", and that ultimately, there was a wider goal.

He said: "We need to make sure that trees are recognised, cared for and protected so that they can continue to support wildlife and communities for generations to come."

articles.title: Five killed as Kyiv and Moscow trade strikes, Russia hits second bridge
articles.summary: Russia has also attacked another key bridge in Kyiv, the second such strike in two days.
articles.body:
At least five people have been killed in a series of long-range strikes carried out by Kyiv and Moscow.

Russia attacked a Liberian-flagged ship in Ukraine’s Odesa region, killing one person and injuring three, the Ukrainian Sea Ports Authority said on Saturday in a statement on Telegram. Another 12 crew members were safely evacuated from the ship. Three were injured.

Russia has in effect blockaded Ukraine’s Black Sea ports – formerly a key global source of food exports – by attacking civilian vessels carrying grain and steel, dealing a heavy blow to the Ukrainian economy.

Two people were reportedly killed in a Ukrainian strike on the Russia-occupied Luhansk region of Ukraine, according to the Moscow-installed governor.

In the occupied Zaporizhia region, Russian-installed authorities said one person was killed and 10 others injured in a Ukrainian drone attack.

Russian media also reported that one person was killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Russia’s Belgorod region, which sits just across the border from Ukraine.

Elsewhere, a Russian attack on Kyiv’s Northern Bridge injured two people. It is the second bridge Russia has attacked in the Ukrainian capital in the space of two days.

Also on Saturday, Russia’s Foreign Ministry issued another warning to diplomats and foreigners in Ukraine’s capital, urging them to leave the city or risk being harmed.

Many foreign embassies are still operating in Kyiv.

Russia’s all-out war on Ukraine is in its fifth year and shows little sign of slowing down.

Russian battlefield gains have slowed to a near-record low, with Ukrainian counterattacks, including one ongoing push around the town of Lyman in the east, mitigating Russian territorial gains elsewhere.

Russia has increased its attacks on civilian infrastructure in recent months, including with the growing use of jet-powered long-range strike drones, which move faster and are harder to shoot down.

Ukraine has also engaged in significant long-range strikes, including targeting Russian oil infrastructure and military-industrial facilities deep inside Russian territory.

articles.title: JACK CARR: The lesson from FlyDubai is simple. Be ready to save yourself
articles.summary: The FlyDubai Flight 1073 knife attack over Saudi Arabia exposes critical gaps in pilot screening and cockpit security that demand new reforms.
articles.body: The events on FlyDubai Flight 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv on 30 September 2026 reads like something out of one of my thrillers. But what occurred in the skies over Saudi Arabia was not fiction, it was real world and highlights an adage I learned long ago and has been repeated in various incarnations across social channels with differing attributions over the years — hope is not a course of action, in most cases, no one is coming to save you, you will need to be your own cavalry. That means be prepared. I am actually surprised that this or something like this has not happened previously — an unhinged pilot or co-pilot killing the other, perhaps suicidal, perhaps in search of martyrdom, as what some terrorist organizations call an istishhadi or "martyrdom seeker." FORMER ISRAELI PM HAILS ‘HEROISM’ AFTER PASSENGERS HELP THWART ALLEGED COCKPIT ATTACK With prior planning it is possible for pilots to work together in a "martyrdom operation" that would be much harder to thwart. Or a single pilot or co-pilot could work with other "muscle" sitting in first class to prevent passengers from doing what they did on September 30, giving the terrorist in the cockpit time to kill them all or once again turn an airliner into a weapon focused on a specific target. I think about scenarios like this every time I fly. I look at and evaluate the passengers, the flight attendants, and I always look in on the pilots as I enter the aircraft, searching for anything that does not look or feel right, remembering something a Vietnam-era Project Delta Army Special Forces soldier told me decades ago: "if it doesn’t look right, it’s probably not." Trust your instincts — you have them for a reason. I am also identifying assets and liabilities among those groups. Who is a potential asset if things go south? I’m noting shoes, belts, shirts, watches, hats, bags, sunglasses, tattoos, cauliflower ear, and filing away what that tells me about each person. Which of them are likely to help — and which of them may hinder in the event of an incident. On September 30, the skies over Saudi Arabia were full of miracles. The pilot, Captain Smit Machchhar, was not immediately incapacitated in the initial knife attack and managed to open the cockpit door before collapsing. Passengers with the instinct to act, fight, and prevail were sitting near the front of the plane, one of the passengers had the wherewithal to pull back on the controls — something he remembered from watching a television show. HERO FLYDUBAI PILOT SAYS HE WAS 'FIGHTING FOR MY LIFE' AS PLANE PLUNGED AFTER COPILOT ATTACK And there happened to be a pilot or pilots onboard who were able land the plane. Incredible. If any one of those things had not happened, we would be talking about a very different incident, one in which every single person on that flight is dead. I weave a lot of history and the history of terrorism into my thrillers, and I also have a series of non-fiction books on terrorism, the second of which is on Pan Am 103, a plane that exploded over Lockerbie, Scotland, on December 21, 1988, killing 259 passengers and crew and 11 residents on the ground. In that attack, there was no warning — a bomb detonated in the cargo hold at 31,000 feet. The destruction of Pan Am 103 horrified the world — and led to important changes in airline security, thanks in large part to pressure from victims’ families who pushed lawmakers to pass the Aviation Security Improvement Act of 1990. That legislation heightened the focus on domestic and international security, including placing federal security managers at major airports and requiring background checks on all air carrier workers. The law demanded the FAA work in tandem with the FBI, expanded scrutiny of overseas airports, and improved the flow of terrorist threat information. AMERICA BUILT A FORTRESS AFTER 9/11. THEN THE THREAT STARTED HIDING IN PLAIN SIGHT The recent FlyDubai event should lead to changes as well, namely enhanced pilot screenings. It is not just about qualifications and your ability to fly a plane — it’s about your background, associations, and your mental stability. If, for example, a background check finds that instead of funding your 401(k) each month, you are diverting funds to Hezbollah or a charity funding terrorist organizations — an obvious red flag — you should not be a pilot and certainly should not be flying a plane full of Israelis into Tel Aviv. This is common sense to most, but common sense seems to be in limited supply these days. The model for hijackings and the use of terror focused on airlines was different before September 11, 2001. Typically, in the 1970s and 1980s, planes were hijacked and the passengers were exchanged for prisoners or ransomed — sometimes a passenger or passengers were killed to make a point. articles.title: Ethiopian gov’t forces advance in Tigray as rebels retreat: What to know
articles.summary: Military, pro-government forces recapture airport in Tigray’s capital as fighting also rages in Amhara and Afar regions.
articles.body:
Ethiopia’s military and pro-government forces have recaptured the main airport in Mekelle , the capital of Tigray, as the government forces advanced in the northern region after more than a week of intense fighting.

Fighting erupted last week between the federal government of Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) and its allies, shattering the fragile Pretoria Agreement, a peace deal signed in November 2022.

The fighting has stoked fears that it could escalate into a wider regional conflict, potentially drawing in neighbouring countries in the Horn of Africa.

This is what you need to know about the latest developments:

Ethiopian troops regained control of Alula Aba Nega Airport in Mekelle, a source with knowledge of the events in the city and a humanitarian source told the Reuters news agency.

The airport, about ⁠10km (6 miles) east of the centre of Mekelle, was one of three airfields in the region that were seized by rebel forces at the start of the fighting on September 23.

A third source, a Mekelle resident who asked not to be named for security reasons, confirmed government forces had retaken the airport and added that gunfire could be heard outside the city centre.

This source reported seeing some fighters from the TPLF abandoning their posts and heading home and said looting of government facilities was taking place in the city.

This was also confirmed by a local journalist who told the AFP news agency the “TPLF militants and leaders are leaving Mekelle.”

The journalist added that government offices and police stations had also been left without security personnel.

A local resident told AFP that he was concerned “government and public property could be exposed to looting”.

“Lawlessness could spread in the city, and I am also afraid for my life. I want us to quickly return to law and order,” another resident said.

On Friday, Al Jazeera’s bureau chief in Ethiopia, Mohammed Taha Tawakel, reported that forces loyal to the federal government have made significant gains in Tigray, taking control of several towns and closing in on Mekelle.

The fighting has occurred on several fronts across northern Ethiopia that stretch across the Tigray, Amhara and Afar regions.

Last week, the Tigray Peace Force, an armed group composed of Tigrayan fighters aligned with the federal government, said it had captured the town of Alamata.

Alamata is important because it sits near Tigray’s southern border with Amhara and serves as a supply hub for troops, fuel and food. Control of the town could allow federal forces to push north towards Mekelle.

The offensive in Afar could threaten supply routes from Djibouti, through which most Ethiopian imports, including fuel, pass.

The fighting in Afar also comes amid allegations of direct Eritrean involvement.

Ethiopia has accused Eritrea of backing armed groups opposed to its government. Eritrea has rejected the accusations

Fighting has also spread into Amhara , including around North Wollo. The Ethiopian military has said about 270 Tigrayan fighters have been killed and more than 200 wounded there.

Outside northern Ethiopia, the conflict appeared to spill into the capital, Addis Ababa, for the first time early on Thursday as an explosion was reported at the Ministry of Defence.

What is the humanitarian situation like?

The fighting is already taking a devastating humanitarian toll.

At least 52 civilians have been killed due to fighting in northern Ethiopia.

Doctors Without Borders, also known by its French acronym MSF, said last week that there had been a surge in the number of wounded in the north.

Amnesty International said on Friday that since the fighting has restarted, it has received “credible reports of destruction of civilian objects through shelling and air strikes, intensified forced conscription, and other acts that may constitute violations of international humanitarian law and international human rights law”.

“The African Union’s Peace and Security Council cannot wait for mass atrocities to unfold or for a surge in civilian casualties before placing Ethiopia, its host country, on the agenda. The AU, which was one of the guarantors of the ceasefire agreement that has now effectively collapsed, must learn from past mistakes and urgently activate its response mechanisms and mobilize its member states before it is too late,” Tigere Chagutah, Amnesty International’s regional director for East and Southern Africa, said in a statement.

“The starting point is for the Peace and Security Council to urgently convene an emergency session on the situation in Ethiopia. This is especially critical as fears of regionalisation of the conflict are on the rise ”.

Analysts fear the current conflict could spread beyond Ethiopia’s borders.

On Thursday, Eritrea cut off diplomatic relations with Ethiopia, escalating a long-simmering conflict between the two states.

In a statement, Eritrea’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said Ethiopia’s actions had left it with “no option but to reciprocate in kind and sever all diplomatic ties with Ethiopia”.

The ministry accused Ethiopia of pursuing a years-long “agenda of incessant hostility”, including by infringing on its coastal areas and arming fighters opposed to Ethiopia’s government.

Eritrea and Ethiopia restored ties in 2018 under Abiy’s leadership after more than 20 years of tensions, but their relations have since soured over Addis Ababa’s accusation that Asmara backs the Tigray rebels.

Ethiopia and Eritrea now also find themselves on opposing sides.

Conflict in their shared neighbour, Sudan, has drawn in both countries, alongside other states in Africa and the Gulf.

Down the coast, Somalia’s security crises are deepening, threatening to fragment the country further as foreign powers eye its self-governing regions for their coastline.

Against this backdrop, the United States-Israel war on Iran and the involvement of Yemen’s Houthis just across the Red Sea from Eritrea have also increased concerns over trade routes through that waterway.

Laura Hammond, professor in development studies at SOAS University of London, told Al Jazeera on Friday that this scenario is already under way.

“The risks that conflict will spread to other countries or that neighbours in the region will be brought into the present conflict are already playing out in terms of Eritrea’s support for the TPLF and the Alliance for Survival,” Hammond said.

“There is a strong possibility that Eritrea will become more involved in the conflict on the ground inside Tigray if it continues much longer,” she continued. “There is also a risk that the conflict could inflame relations with and inside Sudan.”

Eritrea has denied it is involved in the war.

articles.title: Mum of baby found on Bangor shoreline urged to call special number
articles.summary: Police searching for the mother of a newborn girl whose body was found urge her to contact them.
articles.body:
Police searching for the mother of a newborn baby girl whose body was found on a north Wales shoreline have set up a special phone line, urging her to contact them.

A member of the public found the body on the Menai Strait shoreline near Siliwen Road in Bangor, Gwynedd, on Sunday shortly before 17:00 BST.

In an update on Thursday , North Wales Police said a post-mortem examination revealed the newborn was a girl, adding that she may have been in the water for up to a few weeks.

Supt Llinos Davies from North Wales Police said a specialist would take a call from the woman directly and could support her confidentially and told the woman not to be afraid to speak to the police.

"We understand that you may be scared to come forward, but we urge you to contact us," Davies said.

"I want to reassure you that your welfare and safety continues to be our priority and utmost concern and that you receive any medical attention and support you may need.

"Whatever has happened, you do not have to face this on your own," she added.

The director of midwifery and women's services for Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board Fiona Giraud last week also appealed directly to the mother to come forward.

Davies said a trained specialist whose role was "simply to listen, understand, and help" would speak to her.

"This is not a conversation you need to be afraid of. You will be treated with compassion, dignity and respect.

"If making that call feels too difficult, please consider telling somebody you trust. A friend, family member, neighbour, healthcare professional, or anyone who can help you reach out."

The phone number is to strictly only be used by the mother to seek specialist help, North Wales Police said.

"We are concerned the baby's mother may not be in a position to reach out for support, so we are appealing directly to her, the father and those who may have knowledge, such as friends, family, neighbours or colleagues, to contact us," Davies said.

She added that all names provided would be treated "with the utmost discretion" and urges people not to speculate on the circumstances surrounding the baby's death.

Officers are appealing to anyone who routinely walked in the Siliwen Road and Ashley Fields areas of Bangor between 30 August and 27 September to come forward.

They are also asking for any photos or videos taken in and around the Menai Straits shoreline in Siliwen within the same time frame to be uploaded to the force's major incident public portal.

articles.title: Britain’s military in Kenya: Allegations, immunity and a fight for justice
articles.summary: Kenyan survivors are challenging the UK military over decades of alleged abuses — and the immunity that has shielded it.
articles.body:
When Noldonyo Piro and her older sister were growing up, they were inseparable. Just a year apart, Piro, then about 15, and Mantoi Lekoloi Kaunda, 16, spent most days grazing the family’s herd of about 250 goats and sheep across the vast plains that stretch for miles around their home in northern Kenya.

“We lived a very simple life,” Piro, now in her 40s, recalls, sitting outside her small home made of tin sheets and sticks, topped with a patchwork roof of plastic bags in Archer’s Post, a rural settlement in Samburu County.

“I remember we used to stand some distance away from each other, and then one of us would start singing, and the other would answer. We loved to play with each other and tell stories.”

As teenagers in the mid-1990s, their biggest fears involved the wildlife roaming the area — lions, cheetahs and elephants. The sisters had no reason to fear the British soldiers who had long trained on the outskirts of Archer’s Post. In fact, neither had ever seen a white man before — until, on one afternoon, everything changed.

Piro and Mantoi, who was about six months pregnant, were out herding livestock when Piro saw white soldiers approaching from behind.

“I felt scared and started running,” she tells Al Jazeera, staring at the thickets across the arid landscape. “One of them chased me and hit me on the back of my head.”

“I fell down, and the soldier stood on my arm until it snapped and broke.” She holds up the arm, still visibly indented where the bone broke.

Piro says the soldier then raped her until she passed out. When she regained consciousness, she was covered in blood. Nearby, her sister Mantoi lay with her eyes closed, lifeless.

Piro staggered home. “She was just shouting ‘problem, problem,’ and I could see she was having trouble walking,” her father, the late Kaunda Lekoloi, later told ITV. “She said the white men had attacked them.”

“I found Mantoi covered in blood. I could see that she was dead. There were two sets of soldiers’ boot prints in the dust.”

He carried his daughter’s body home on a donkey and buried her the next morning.

No police post was within reach, and for a Samburu pastoralist in the 1990s, reporting an attack by men in foreign uniforms was unlikely to lead anywhere.

For years the family lived with the horror in silence, only whispered from household to household.

“After that day, I became more scared of white men than I was of lions,” Piro says, her eyes filling with tears. “Even now, when I think about what happened, it makes me sick to my stomach.”

No one has ever been charged over Mantoi’s alleged murder.

Her case is among decades of allegations against soldiers from the British Army Training Unit Kenya, or BATUK, that include rape, murder, abandoned children fathered by soldiers, deaths and severe injuries from unexploded ordnance, environmental destruction and fatal vehicle collisions.

The military arrangement dates back to a 1964 defence agreement, signed months after Kenya’s independence, that allowed United Kingdom forces to keep training on Kenyan soil.

Six decades later, BATUK remains embedded in northern Kenya, training around 10,000 soldiers a year in Laikipia and Samburu. There has been no known case in which British personnel accused in the cases documented by Kenyan communities and investigators have faced prosecution in Kenya.

The UK has repeatedly invoked sovereign immunity — the principle that one state cannot be sued in another’s courts — a claim that went untested for decades, keeping cases from reaching Kenyan judges.

Now, finally, that power imbalance is being challenged.

articles.title: Alison Hammond returns home from hospital after rushing off This Morning
articles.summary: The This Morning presenter said she believes she experienced a panic attack on Friday's show.
articles.body:
Alison Hammond has said she is home and "feeling so much better" after she went to hospital for a heart check-up after leaving ITV's This Morning midway through Friday's show.

The presenter, 51, left the programme during its live broadcast, appearing to clutch her chest as she was helped off set by co-host Dermot O'Leary. He later told viewers she was "feeling a little unwell".

Soon after Hammond said she had "a little bit of a palpitation" and was undergoing tests.

In a video on Instagram on Saturday, she said she was "all OK, all-clear, which would mean I had a massive panic attack on live TV. I mean, the shame of it."

Alison Hammond has heart check-up in hospital after rushing off This Morning while on air

"It felt very real to me. I'm really new to panic attacks, so I need to learn more about it," she added.

The Birmingham-born presenter, who also co-hosts The Great British Bake Off , thanked NHS staff and her colleagues at This Morning, including O'Leary.

"It's really warmed my heart actually. I didn't necessarily want to be on the news or anything like that but this is a new world to me," she said.

"I'm going to take stock, take some rest and I'll see you soon."

Friday's edition of the ITV show began at 10:00 BST with Hammond and her regular co-host O'Leary at the helm, before she left at 11:30 during a segment about pets.

O'Leary, 53, addressed her absence when the show returned from a break, saying: "Welcome back to This Morning, Alison is feeling a little unwell, so she's just had to duck out. Hopefully she'll be back."

He later updated viewers that she would, in fact, not be returning, "so I'll be here for the rest of the show".

Hammond rose to fame as contestant on Channel 4 reality show Big Brother before appearing on I'm A Celebrity and Strictly Come Dancing.

She became a co-host in This Morning in 2021, and was part of the team that won a National Television Award for best daytime programme the following year.

She joined Bake Off in 2023 and took over from the late Paul O'Grady on For the Love of Dogs in 2024.
